about.title: Woodlake Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Woodlake is a small city, but its traffic still moves through a handful of busy corridors — Avenue 344, Valencia Boulevard, Rt 216, and Main Street chief among them. Public collision counts show reports tend to cluster around Friday evenings, when work and weekend traffic overlap on these roads. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: photos of the vehicles and scene, contact information for witnesses, and a prompt medical evaluation can all shape how a claim is handled later. We handle car accident claims directly in Tulare County and can review what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee owed unless we recover money on your behalf. The sooner details are preserved, the more there is to work with.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than It Seems
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window can drop to as little as six months if a government vehicle or road defect was involved. We can spot that distinction early, before it costs you your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Your Story Matters
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces what you can collect. How the crash is documented and described can directly affect that percentage, which is why early evidence matters.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash — you're not required to give one, and it can be used to minimize your claim later. We can handle that conversation for you instead.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Avenue 344 near Woodlake — do I still have a case if the police report says nothing?
items.answer: A police report is one piece of evidence, but it isn't required to pursue a claim. Photos, medical records, witness accounts, and the vehicle damage itself can all help establish what happened. We can look at what you do have and tell you where you stand.

items.question: Is there a charge to talk to an attorney about my case?
items.answer: No. There's no charge for an initial case review. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a city or county road in Woodlake and involved a public vehicle?
items.answer: Claims involving government vehicles or agencies in California often have a much shorter deadline — sometimes just six months instead of two years. It's worth having this reviewed quickly rather than waiting, since missing that window can end a claim before it starts.
